## Known facts
- **No input drift detected.** `check_prediction_drift` read both API Pods (`wine-quality-api-5b9dffd57c-htjv9`, `...zv5g9`) over the window since each Pod started, found 60 predictions, and used model version **6** (the deployed version) as the baseline against run `c52f21d3155f488ab33b38dc860ca0ea`.
- Every feature's live mean sits within 0.5 std of its training mean, so none crossed the drift threshold: the largest shift is **chlorides at −0.21σ** (live 0.0493 vs training 0.0572) and **volatile_acidity at −0.17σ**. All flagged `drifted: false`.
- **Positive-prediction rate is elevated:** live predictions are positive **28.3%** of the time versus a training label rate of **18.9%**. This is the one mismatch, but it is a *label-rate* difference, not an input-feature shift.

## Uncertainties
- The tool measures **input drift only** — it cannot tell you whether live predictions are actually more or less accurate, because that requires ground-truth labels, which aren't available here.
- The positive-rate gap could be benign (e.g., a different slice of real traffic than the training set) or a signal worth watching; this check alone can't classify it.
- Drift is measured against **Pod start time**, so it covers only the current deployment window, not all historical traffic.

## Recommended actions
No retraining is indicated by input drift — the features match training well enough. If you want to understand the positive-rate gap, pull a sample of live predictions with their true labels and compare accuracy directly; otherwise, treat this as a monitor item rather than an action item.
